problems.source_says: AI adoption is the maximum SBERT cosine similarity between each submitted idea and the AI example ideas that were on the same screen while the person wrote it. The form itself codes ai_available_when_produced 'yes' and construct 'other'. Codebook section 1 then gives with_ai: 'An outcome produced with AI available is across_people when its construct is diversity and with_ai otherwise.' The codebook has no 'none' code. The form-spec allows 'none' for outcomes that answer none of the three questions, and its example is AI output compared with human output. This measure is computed on ideas that people wrote. The form also applies the rule unevenly: S1-O5 (local idea diversity) is the same kind of SBERT distance between the submitted idea and the examples shown, with the same construct and the same AI availability, and the form codes it with_ai. If the screeners judge that AI adoption answers none of the questions, form-spec rule 7 does not call for listing it, and the result belongs in notes. Fix: recode to with_ai, or drop S1-O6 and keep the result in notes. The stakes are small, because the paper calls the outcome secondary and does not interpret its main effect of condition.
problems.quote: We operationalized AI adoption as the maximum similarity (following Roemmele [67]) between a submitted idea and AI example ideas a participant saw.

problems.form_value: Six contrasts: the four AI arms against Control, plus HighExposureDisclosed-HighExposureUndisclosed and LowExposureDisclosed-LowExposureUndisclosed. No High-versus-Low exposure contrast.
problems.source_says: Tables 11 to 13 print ten contrasts each. Rows 5 and 8 compare High with Low exposure at a fixed disclosure level. Table 12 (median): HighExposureDisclosed-LowExposureDisclosed 0.74, adj p 0.001, Cliff's delta 0.23, and HighExposureUndisclosed-LowExposureUndisclosed 1.41, 0.001, 0.29. Table 11 (mean pairwise): 1.00, 0.001, 0.29 and 1.36, 0.001, 0.28. Table 13 (centroid): 1.12, 0.001, 0.29 and 1.46, 0.001, 0.28. These are ai_design contrasts of the kind codebook section 5 lists ('one idea versus five'), and the paper's headline finding is about the exposure level ('high AI exposure (but not low AI exposure)'). The form takes the two disclosure rows from the same tables but not these two rows. Rows 6 and 7 change exposure and disclosure together and can stay out. This is minor: no coded value is wrong, but the record is incomplete.

confirmed: S1-O1 and S1-O2 score each submitted idea with the fine-tuned GPT-3 classifier of Organisciak et al. This is a computed score, not a self-report. The paper says the classifier measures originality, so construct novelty and measure automated_score hold (p. 3, Section 1.2.1; p. 11, Section 6.4, 'the classifier measures one facet of creativity: originality'; p. 13, Appendix A.1).

AI ideas were on screen while each idea was written. Participants ranked six example ideas (two or four from ChatGPT in the AI arms) and typed their own idea on the same page. So ai_available_when_produced 'yes' and timing 'immediate' hold for every S1 outcome. No outcome is produced after AI is removed, so no after_ai record is missing (p. 2, Figure 1; p. 5, Section 3.4.3; p. 16, Figure 12).

S1-O3 and S1-O4 compare ideas from different people. Each person does each condition and each item once, so a condition-item pool, and an (item, condition, trial number) pool, holds at most one idea per person. Construct diversity and question across_people hold (p. 5, Section 3.4.2 and Figure 2; pp. 14-15, Appendix B.2 and B.3; p. 21, SI 8.1; p. 25, SI 8.3).

Units are the paper's own: one row per submitted idea for creativity, local diversity, and AI adoption (3,271, 3,271, and 2,618 observations), 50-idea samples of each condition-item pool over 50 Monte Carlo runs for global diversity, and 362 pool-level rows for the evolution of diversity (p. 26, Table 18; p. 23, Table 14; p. 28, Table 22; p. 21, SI 8.1; p. 25, Table 17).

S1-O1 numbers match the PDF text layer: LoExposure_Disclosed 0.011 (0.112), t = 0.095; LoExposure_Undisclosed 0.019 (0.112), t = 0.166; HiExposure_Disclosed -0.025 (0.113), t = -0.221; HiExposure_Undisclosed 0.050 (0.113), t = 0.443; 3,271 observations; joint test F(4, 19.86) = 0.12, p = 0.97 (p. 26, Table 18; p. 8, Section 5.4).
S1-O2 matches: the likelihood ratio test for the trial number x condition interaction gives chi2(4) = 6.52, p = 0.16 (p. 8, Section 5.4; p. 15, Appendix B.3).

S1-O3 numbers match Tables 11 to 13 for all six coded contrasts, for example Table 12 HighExposureDisclosed-Control 1.21, 0.001, 0.31 and LowExposureUndisclosed-Control -0.61, 0.0063, -0.06 (p. 21, Table 11; p. 22, Tables 12 and 13).

Figure 7 is titled 'Error bars are 95% CIs'. It plots Low Exposure Undisclosed (about 81.8) below Control (about 82.4) and Low Exposure Disclosed (about 82.9) above it. So the form is right to follow Table 12 over the p. 8 sentence that gives Low Exposure Undisclosed the higher diversity (p. 7, Figure 7; p. 8, Section 5.2).

S1-O4 numbers match: Table 17 column (1) interactions 0.140 (0.231), 0.368 (0.233), 0.525 (0.239), and 0.566 (0.239); control slope -0.391 (0.175); 362 observations; text beta = 0.53, 95% CI [0.06, 0.99] and beta = 0.57, 95% CI [0.1, 1.03] (p. 25, Table 17; p. 8, Section 5.3).

S1-O5 numbers match: F(4, 19.95) = 0.09, p = 0.98, and Table 14 column (1) condition rows -1.467 (1.864), 0.272 (1.861), 1.051 (1.864), and -0.744 (1.866), with 3,271 observations. Construct 'other' is defensible: in the AI arms two or four of the six comparison ideas are ChatGPT ideas, so the measure does not compare people's outputs only (p. 23, SI 8.2 and Table 14; p. 2, Figure 1).

S2-O1 matches Table 6: sourcechatgpt 0.618 (0.027), Constant 2.751 (0.029), 3,000 observations; text beta = 0.62, t(2994) = 22.49, 95% CI [0.56, 0.67]. Question 'none' fits the form-spec example of AI output compared with human output (p. 19, SI 4 and Table 6).

No outcome is self-reported. Self-perceived creativity, perceived AI creativity, and AI attitude are pre-treatment answers that enter only as covariates and moderators (p. 5, Section 3.4.1; p. 6, Figure 4; p. 14, Appendix B.1).

No other outcome that bears on the three questions is missing. The uniqueness and ranking-accuracy scores were feedback to participants, with no analysis by condition. Tables 15, 16, 20, and 21 and Figure 10 re-estimate local diversity or AI adoption in subgroups (p. 19, SI 5; p. 24, Tables 15-16; pp. 27-28, Tables 20-21; p. 9, Figure 10).
summary: The form codes c002's outcomes correctly in substance: every outcome is a classifier or SBERT score of the submitted ideas, AI examples were on screen when each idea was written, the units match the paper's analyses, and every reported number matches the PDF (Tables 6, 11-14, 17, 18, and 22; pp. 7-9). The conclusion is still refuted, because S1-O6 (AI adoption) is coded question 'none' where the codebook rule gives with_ai, as the form itself does for the parallel S1-O5, and S1-O3 omits the High-versus-Low exposure contrasts that Tables 11 to 13 print (a minor gap).
